question.worked_solution:
Given a set of $n$ paired observations ${x}_{1},{x}_{2},…,{x}_{n}$ and ${y}_{1},{y}_{2},…,{y}_{n},$ the sum of squared deviations from the mean for the data ${y}_{i}$ can be calculated as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}{S}_{yy} & ={\sum }_{i=1}^{n}({y}_{i}-\overset{―}{y})^{2} \\  & ={\sum }_{i}{y}_{i}^{2}-\frac{1}{n}{({\sum }_{i=1}^{n}{y}_{i})}^{2}\end{aligned}
$$

First, we calculate the sum of the ${y}_{i}$ data:

$$
{\sum }_{i=1}^{6}{y}_{i}=12+13+16+14+14+15=84.
$$

We are given that ${\sum }_{i=1}^{6}{y}_{i}^{2}=1\,186.$

Finally, by substituting into the above formula, we get

$$
{S}_{yy}=1\,186-\frac{1}{6}(84)^{2}=1\,186-1\,176=10.
$$
